requirement: The first edition incorporates the formal definitions of the Base Class, Extended Numerics and Extended Array libraries from ECMA-335 first edition, December 2001, Partition IV.
notes: First-edition clause 3 and normative Annex D supply this dated incorporation. ISO-1 follows the second edition and its ECMA-335 second-edition incorporation. These bindings permit implementation extensions; concrete C# construct dependencies have their own rules.

requirement: The dated ISO 31.11:1992 reference supplies the incorporated normative mathematical signs and symbols; subsequent amendments or revisions do not apply under the first edition's dated-reference policy.
notes: The first edition incorporates ISO 31.11:1992 under its dated-reference policy. The seventh edition incorporates the undated ISO 80000-2 reference under its latest-edition policy. Concrete language dependencies have their own rules; this reference does not forbid implementation extensions.

requirement: The dated ISO/IEC 2382.1:1993 reference supplies the incorporated normative fundamental vocabulary; subsequent amendments or revisions do not apply under the first edition's dated-reference policy.
notes: The first edition incorporates ISO/IEC 2382.1:1993 under its dated-reference policy. The seventh edition incorporates the undated ISO/IEC 2382 reference under its latest-edition policy. Concrete language dependencies have their own rules; this reference does not forbid implementation extensions.

requirement: ISO/IEC 10646, all parts, is a separate incorporated normative character-set authority, and its undated reference is governed by the latest-edition policy.
notes: The first edition separately incorporates ISO/IEC 10646, all parts, under its undated-reference policy. The seventh edition has no separate ISO/IEC 10646 entry in clause 2. The incorporation does not forbid implementation extensions.

requirement: The dated IEC 60559:1989 reference supplies the incorporated normative binary floating-point authority; subsequent amendments or revisions do not apply under the first edition's dated-reference policy.
notes: The first edition incorporates IEC 60559:1989 under its dated-reference policy; the accompanying IEEE designation names the same authority. The seventh edition incorporates ISO/IEC 60559:2020. Concrete floating-point language requirements have their own rules.

requirement: The first edition's normative Unicode reference names The Unicode Standard, Version 3.0 as defined by its 2000 book together with Unicode Technical Report 15, Unicode Normalization Forms; the first edition's conformance permission for Unicode 3.0 or later still applies.
notes: The first edition incorporates its Unicode 3.0 book and normalization reference together. Its conformance clause permits Unicode 3.0 or later. The seventh edition uses an undated Unicode reference. Concrete lexical requirements have their own rules.

requirement: The second edition incorporates the formal library definitions from ECMA-335 second edition, December 2002, Partition IV, including the Base Class, Extended Numerics and Extended Array libraries.
notes: This incorporation governs ISO-1. The dated reference supplies the formal definitions and does not forbid implementation extensions.

requirement: The normative Unicode reference includes Technical Report 19 on UTF-32 alongside the Unicode Standard, Version 3.0 and Technical Report 15 on normalization.
notes: Clause 2 permits Unicode 3.0 or later; this reference supplies no blanket ban on characters assigned in a later Unicode version.

requirement: The third edition incorporates the formal definitions of the Base Class, Extended Numerics and Extended Array libraries from ISO/IEC 23271:2005, Partition IV.
notes: The fourth edition incorporates the same dated publication in clause 3, p. 5 (PDF p. 27), and governs ISO-2. Subsequent amendments or revisions do not apply.
